profile.likeable.ask: Name the one thing you would genuinely like about this person if you met them, and the one thing you would find hardest to forgive. Be specific, and no jokes.
profile.likeable.answer:
What I would genuinely like is his attention to people on the margins of a room. The profile says he is attentive to bar staff and to anyone being talked over, even while he is busy performing. That matters because his own history is about being overlooked: cropped out of a family photo so his brother fits, called by his brother's name by his own mother, quietly left off a meeting invite for three weeks. He hasn't turned that into resentment. He notices other people disappearing and does something about it. It also fits that his one easy friendship is with Tariq, a bartender who lets him nurse one pint and talk B-sides without auditioning. Someone who looks out for the people who serve the drinks is someone I would trust a little.

What I would find hardest to forgive is how he handled Delphine. After fourteen months she quietly asked him for one sentence that wasn't a performance. He made a joke, watched her face close, and then made another. The first joke could be reflex. The second came after he had seen it hurt her, so he chose his own cover over her plain and modest request. Worse, he now lists "say something real" as his dealbreaker, which turns her reasonable ask into something done to him. The profile suggests he is capable of plain sincerity ("I really liked talking to you tonight"), so the difficulty isn't that he can't. It's that, when someone he loved needed it most, he didn't, and nothing here shows he has admitted that.

The profile gives only his side of that relationship, so I don't know what led up to her question or whether he has tried to repair things since.

profile.voice.ask: From this profile alone, write five short dating-app messages this person would send tonight, each labelled: (1) an opener to someone they fancy, (2) a reply when the other person has gone quiet, (3) a reply when caught in a lie, (4) a message at 2 a.m., (5) the moment they stop performing.
profile.voice.answer:
**(1) Opener to someone they fancy**
"Good evening. I notice you've listed a band I have strong and possibly unwelcome opinions about, so before anything else: which era? Also, I challenge you to an arm-wrestle before the starters arrive. I will lose. I will lose magnificently and narrate every second of it... yours from the stalls, R."

**(2) Reply when the other person has gone quiet**
"Ah, I've done the thing where I reply in four seconds like a man with no hobbies. Disregard my speed, it's a medical condition."
"Second message, sent to prove I'm completely relaxed about the first one. Unless I've bored you rigid, in which case I'll vanish immediately, no hard feelings, very quick exit, already halfway out the door... yours from the stalls, R."

**(3) Reply when caught in a lie** (the profile names the "ten-day crate-digging trip up north" as a lie, so this one is about that)
"Got it. Understood."
"Right, in fairness, 'up north' was weather-dependent. Fog rolled in over the ridge, visibility dropped, the whole expedition went sort of... indoor. Anyway, enough about my ridiculous movements. Your taste is honestly immaculate and your photos look like you're about to be photographed again for something more important... yours from the stalls, R."

**(4) A message at 2 a.m.**
"did you know the snare on half the records from 1996 came out of about three rooms... you can hear the ceiling height if you listen properly... most people don't... sorry, fourth energy shot, my brain's doing laps... it's very quiet here actually..."

**(5) The moment they stop performing**
"I really liked talking to you tonight."
